Messages.Author: Raptor
Messages.Body:
The question is:

One of my vampires calls a vote, it passes and then I throw
a Cryptic Rider down with another vote card. Does the new vote card
"pass automatically"?? My feeling is it does but several of my
fellow players disagree. Please settle this dispute.

Thanks,

Raptor

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Raptor writes:

>The question is:



No. You have to call the vote with another vampire successfully (that is,
without being blocked). A blocked attempt will not "use up" the automatic
pass, however, if you can get another vampire through.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
In article <486bod$j...@charm.magnus.acs.ohio-state.edu>, Raptor writes:

> One of my vampires calls a vote, it passes and then I throw
>a Cryptic Rider down with another vote card. Does the new vote card
>"pass automatically"?? My feeling is it does but several of my
>fellow players disagree. Please settle this dispute.
>

CR makes the next vote pass automatically, but it does not call the vote.
Another vampire must call a vote successfully; if so, THEN that vote
passes.

Messages.Body:

The new vote actually has to be called for it to pass . This has
to be done as an action by another vamp . If this action is blocked the vote
cant , of course , pass . If the (2nd) vote isnt intercepted you dont bother
adding up votes , just assume that it passed . Hmmmmmmm I wonder what this
means with respect to cards whose effects depend on how much a vote passed by .
Can you just not play them in this case ? Any ideas anyone ?

JAC
